sections.html:
Cerro Gordo County runs its government from Mason City, a Winnebago River town in north-central Iowa. Des Moines is about 120 miles south and the Twin Cities about 135 miles north. Clear Lake is a short drive, roughly 8 miles west. The ZIP codes are 50401, 50402 and 50467.

The 2020 count was 27,338 people, down slowly from a high of 30,642 in 1960. Households average 2.07 people and the median age in 2020 was 42.7, so plenty of homes here belong to older owners or are inherited, and many sellers are weighing a move or settling an estate.

These figures cover 2020 to 2024. With homes valued around $142,000 at the median, buyers watch every repair bill, and condition moves price a lot.

sections.h2: Selling a Prairie School or historic house
sections.html:
Few places match Mason City for Prairie School architecture. Rock Crest and Rock Glen Historic District holds at least 32 houses and one commercial building from 1908 to 1922, and 17 are listed on the National Register of Historic Places. Designers include Walter Burley Griffin, Marion Mahony Griffin and Barry Byrne. Frank Lloyd Wright designed the Dr. G.C. Stockman House in 1908, and it was moved four blocks in 1989 to avoid demolition.

Outside those districts the city has Victorian, Craftsman, Bungalow and Mayan Revival homes. Own a house in or beside a historic district? Ask the city before you alter the exterior, and tell any buyer about the historic status up front. An older, unusual house is hard to price from a standard comparable, so expect a wider range of opinions on value.

sections.h2: Selling near the river after the 2008 flood
sections.html:
In June 2008 the Winnebago River reached a record crest of 18.72 feet and overtopped the levee system. The city later ran a voluntary buyout and bought 167 properties, paid for with FEMA hazard mitigation money and HUD community development funds.

Most of the historic houses affected were in the East Park Place area, and five of the 22 individually eligible houses were relocated. East Park Historic District was added to the National Register in 2014. A house close to the river carries that history. Expect buyers to ask about flood insurance and old repairs. Winters are cold here, with an average January high of 24.2 degrees, so roof and furnace condition also get a close look.

sections.h2: Why people stay: parks, jobs and getting around
sections.html:
The municipal park system covers over 600 acres with more than 75 miles of trails. MercyOne North Iowa Medical Center employs over 2,000 people, and healthcare is the biggest job sector. Meredith Willson grew up here, and Music Man Square and the MacNider Art Museum draw visitors.

Iowa 122 and U.S. 65 serve the city, U.S. 18 skirts the south edge, and Interstate 35 lies about 8 miles west. Mason City Municipal Airport has United Airlines flights to Chicago O'Hare. A house near a park or a main road can mention it.

sections.h2: Recording, transfer tax and property tax
sections.html:
The Cerro Gordo County Recorder is at 220 N. Washington Avenue in Mason City, with weekday hours of 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Transfer tax is $1.60 per thousand, and the first $500 is exempt. The Recorder does not keep abstracts, and a replacement can be requested from Cerro Gordo Abstract Company at 641-423-1145. The office cannot help prepare documents, so talk to an attorney about adding or removing a name on a deed.

Statements go out in mid to late August. The September 1 installment goes delinquent on October 1, and the March 1 installment on April 1. Late payments pick up 1.5 percent for each month past due. Unpaid parcels can land in the electronic tax sale held the third Monday in June.

The Treasurer's number is 641-421-3127. Getting a parcel back after a tax sale costs 2 percent per month, paid in guaranteed funds. If you sell while taxes are owed, the closing agent pays them from your proceeds.

sections.h2: Steps from first call to closing
sections.html:
Start by describing the property: address, condition, whether anyone lives there, and any liens or back taxes. We look at the house and the title, then make an offer. If you accept, a title company opens the file and orders a title search to confirm who owns the property and what is owed on it.

You pick the closing date. At the table you sign the deed, the title company pays off any mortgage or tax balance from the proceeds, and you receive the rest. Nothing has to be cleaned out beyond what you agree to, and you do not hold open houses or negotiate with several buyers.

Inherited houses add one step. The person with legal authority over the estate signs, and an attorney can confirm who that is. Houses with a flood history, deferred maintenance or an unusual design are common here, and a cash buyer prices those problems in instead of asking you to fix them.

Bring or send a copy of the deed, the latest property tax statement, the mortgage lender's name and loan number if there is one, and the names of everyone on title. If a name needs to come off or go on, see an attorney first, because the Recorder cannot draft documents for you.

If the house sits in a historic district, add any city correspondence about exterior work. If it was in the East Park Place area, add records of the buyout or repairs after 2008. Clear records shorten the title search and keep the closing date from slipping. If anything is missing, say so early and we will help you track it down through the Recorder or the abstract company.

sections.h2: How a cash sale of a Mason City house works
sections.html:
A cash sale here is short. You describe the house, we look at its condition and its title, and a title company handles the deed and recording if you take the offer. There is no lender, so no loan appraisal can hold things up.

Roof, plumbing or flood repairs do not have to be finished beforehand, which suits an older house. The offer already accounts for them, so weigh it against what a listing might net after repairs, commissions and months of carrying costs. No price is promised in advance, and turning us down costs nothing.

Before closing, gather the deed, your most recent tax statement, any mortgage payoff information and a list of known problems. The closing agent prepares the paperwork and records the deed with the county. Ask for a written payoff figure for any loan so there are no surprises at the table.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Mason City?
faqs.a: Owner-occupied homes carry a median value of $142,000 for 2020 to 2024. Median gross rent is $882.
Yes, in June 2008. The river crested at a record 18.72 feet and went over the levees, and the city later bought out 167 properties.

faqs.q: When are Cerro Gordo County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Half is due September 1 and half March 1. Late status begins October 1 and April 1, and a 1.5 percent monthly penalty applies.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Mason City house in a historic district?
faqs.a: Yes. Ask the city about exterior rules and disclose the historic status. Seventeen houses in Rock Crest and Rock Glen are on the National Register.

faqs.q: What if I owe back taxes when I sell?
faqs.a: The closing agent pays them from your proceeds. Call the Treasurer at 641-421-3127 for the current payoff.
